turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'll go, ma'am, but I hope it's all right with you if I don't call her loudly, I don't want to disturb anyone in the house.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Estella, my child, I find this boy's hesitation... distasteful.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I don't mean to be impolite, ma'am, it's just that I'm not used to being here, and I don't want to get into trouble with my sister

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Estella, show this boy what is meant by 'play', as you have been instructed.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I don't think I can play with Estella, ma'am, because I'm not sure I understand what you mean by 'play' when it involves...when it involves a game, and I don't want to make a mistake.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Foolish boy, do not try to think for yourself. You will play with Estella, and you will play with her as I have instructed.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid I don't know what to play, ma'am, and I don't want to do something wrong

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: I will not be disobeyed, Pip. You will learn to play, and you will play with Estella, as I have decreed. Now, Estella, show him the first lesson.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: But, ma'am, I don't think it's right for me to play with Estella, because...because I'm not sure I'm worthy of such a privilege, and I don't want to take up her time if I'm not good at it.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Silence, boy! You dare to question my judgment? I have decided that you shall play with Estella, and that is final.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid, ma'am, that I don't think I can play with Estella, not without being a burden to her, or doing something wrong, and I would rather not risk that, if it please you

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You foolish boy, you are not worthy of my concern, but you are worthy of my amusement. You will play with Estella, and you will learn to do so with proper decorum, lest you suffer the consequences of my displeasure.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid, ma'am, that I don't know if I can be of any use to Estella in playing, being as I'm not accustomed to such games and might only make a fool of myself, and I wouldn't want to disappoint you

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Silence your doubts, boy, and do as I bid you. I shall teach you the games, and you shall learn to play them with precision and elegance.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm not sure I can play with Estella, ma'am, not if it's going to be one of those games that makes me feel awkward and out of place, and I wouldn't want to make a mistake in front of you or the young lady

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will play with Estella, and you will do it with the precision and elegance that I require. I will not have you making a fool of yourself in my presence, boy. You will be on your best behavior, or suffer the consequences of my displeasure.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm not sure I understand what sort of games you have in mind, ma'am, but I fear I wouldn't be very good at them, and I wouldn't want to disappoint you or Miss Estella

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will play the game, boy, because I say so, and you will not fail me. I have taken a liking to you, and I will not be disappointed.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm not sure, ma'am, I don't think I'm suited for playing games with Estella, she seems so... so refined and I'm just a poor boy from the village

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will play with Estella, boy, because it is my pleasure to see her excel, and I will not be denied the satisfaction of watching you try to keep pace with her.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Come nearer; let me look at you. Come close.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Look at me. You are not afraid of a woman who has never seen the sun since you were born?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Do you know what I touch here?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I am tired. I want diversion, and I have done with men and women. Play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I sometimes have sick fancies, and I have a sick fancy that I want to see some play. There, there!

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: No, ma’am, I am very sorry for you, and very sorry I can’t play just now. If you complain of me I shall get into trouble with my sister, so I would do it if I could; but it’s so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.
